name: Subaru
overview: Subaru built a fiercely loyal following in Australia through boxer engines, symmetrical all-wheel drive, outback rally dominance, and rugged crossover utility.
australian_history:
Subaru's official presence in Australia commenced in 1973 when Frank O'Brien established Subaru Motor Imports (later acquired by global automotive distributor Inchcape in 1992). The early Leone 1400 4WD wagons demonstrated that a compact passenger car could conquer Australian dirt roads and river crossings without the bulk of a heavy truck.

In 1978, Subaru introduced the Brumby (MV ute), a front-engine, selectable-4WD light utility powered by a 1.6L and later 1.8L boxer engine. The Brumby became an instant rural icon across Australian farms, sheep stations, and country towns, celebrated for its lightweight agility, incredible fuel efficiency, and near-indestructible mechanicals.

In 1989, Subaru moved upmarket with the Liberty (known globally as the Legacy), which won the prestigious Wheels Car of the Year award in 1994 and 1998. The compact Impreza arrived in 1993, followed in February 1994 by the revolutionary Impreza WRX. With a 2.0L turbocharged boxer engine and permanent symmetrical all-wheel drive, the WRX democratized supercar performance for under $40,000. New Zealander Peter 'Possum' Bourne piloted the WRX to seven consecutive Australian Rally Championship (ARC) titles from 1996 to 2002, cementing the WRX and STI as performance legends.

In 1996, Subaru created the modern crossover category with the Liberty Outback (later simply Outback), lifting the suspension and adding rugged body cladding. The Forester arrived in 1997, quickly becoming one of Australia's favourite family SUVs. In 1998, Subaru Australia made the bold decision to make All-Wheel Drive standard across its entire passenger car lineup in Australia (excluding subsequent joint-venture rear-drive coupes like the BRZ), a unique market positioning that propelled the brand to record sales. Today, Subaru Australia remains headquartered in Baulkham Hills, NSW under Inchcape Australia.

models.overview: The Subaru Liberty (Legacy globally) and Outback revolutionized Australian family and touring motoring. Spanning seven generations, the Liberty delivered rally-bred AWD performance with the BC RS Turbo, twin-turbo B4, and 2003 Wheels Car of the Year winning BL/BP GT Spec.B, while the lifted Outback pioneered the crossover wagon genre in 1996 and evolved into Australia's ultimate all-road adventure tourer.

liberty-outback.name: Liberty & Outback
liberty-outback.overview: The Subaru Liberty (Legacy globally) and Outback revolutionized Australian family and touring motoring. Spanning seven generations, the Liberty delivered rally-bred AWD performance with the BC RS Turbo, twin-turbo B4, and 2003 Wheels Car of the Year winning BL/BP GT Spec.B, while the lifted Outback pioneered the crossover wagon genre in 1996 and evolved into Australia's ultimate all-road adventure tourer.
liberty-outback.australian_market_notes: First sold in Australia in 1989 (renamed Liberty due to Legacy Australia's veterans' charity trademark), the Liberty won instant respect. Colin McRae and Possum Bourne campaigned the RS Turbo in Australian and Asia-Pacific rallying. In 1996, the Outback created an entirely new market segment. While the Liberty sedan bowed out in 2020 after 31 years and over 153,000 Australian sales, the Outback thrives with the 2.4-litre turbocharged XT.

forester.name: Forester
forester.overview: The Subaru Forester is an Australian automotive legend that helped pioneer the compact all-wheel-drive crossover genre in 1997. Blending permanent Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive, high ground clearance, commanding estate-car visibility, and turbocharged WRX engines in GT and XT badges, it earned an intensely loyal following among Australian families, campers, and rural motorists.
forester.australian_market_notes: Launched in Australia in September 1997, the Forester was an instant sales success. The introduction of the turbo Forester GT in 1998 democratized high-performance all-weather motoring for families, a formula expanded with the SG XT, SH S-Edition, and SJ XT. Across six generations, the Forester has been a fixture of Australian outdoor lifestyle culture.
